newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Algeria happy with Polisario talks - agency.
newsitem.headline: Algeria happy with Polisario talks - agency.

text.p: Algeria's foreign minister said on Tuesday that talks between Morocco and the Polisario Front, who have fought over the Western Sahara, raised "encouragement and satisfaction", Morocco's official news agency MAP said.

In a report from Algiers, the agency quoted the minister, Ahmed Attaf, as saying: "As far as the meetings between the Moroccan authorities and Polisario leaders are concerned, Algeria has...always called for and encouraged the parties to the conflict to promote dialogue and direct negotiations.

"Everything which leads in this direction can only bring on our part support, encouragement and satisfaction because we believe in the need for a political settlement to avoid...the dangers of conflict and also save the region from the dangers of instability."
Morocco has said that it could neither confirm nor deny the talks took place.

A diplomatic source in Rabat who has closely followed the conflict said on Tuesday that a seven-strong Polisario delegation led by the front's number two, Mustapha Bechir Sayed, spent four days in Morocco.
The source said: "They were preliminary talks, attended by Moroccan Crown Prince Sidi Mohammed and Interior Minister Driss Basri. They were aimed at breaking the dealock over the referendum."
Polisario and Morocco fought a desert war in the former Spanish territory -- claimed by Rabat -- for nearly 17 years before a U.N.-brokered ceasefire in September 1991.
A referendum of the Western Sahara's people -- to decide on independence as sought by the Polisario, or integration with Morocco -- was due in January 1992.
Despite U.N. efforts to draw up an electoral role, the vote has been delayed by wrangles over who, among the largely nomadic people, is eligible to take part.
The last direct talks were held in 1989 in the Moroccan city of Marrakesh.
